title: BOUNDED-1 dispatch leaves no task:<id> resume-key lock visible to S2's pipeline-resume duplicate-spawn guard
task_involved: FIX-AUDITOR-DEDUP-TASKBOARD-PRECHECK-NOT-ENFORCED (still live: developer background agent adeb194ad9fffeb25, confirmed running by harness tracking at time of this probe)
evidence: head.status=in_progress, active_task_id=FIX-AUDITOR-DEDUP-TASKBOARD-PRECHECK-NOT-ENFORCED, updated_by='dev-team (bounded-1 auto-pickup)' at 2026-08-06T10:52:20Z (prior 10:37Z tick). This 11:07Z tick's Step 0b resumed pipeline-resume on the same head. task_status resolved IN_PROGRESS (genuinely live, not BLOCKED/terminal/READY), should_hold=false (not supervised) -- per main.md's literal WF-1/WF-1b/WF-1c/WF-2 chain this falls through to S2 dispatcher-wrap, which attempts task_claim(task_id='task:'+id, task_kind=sprint-task, owner_agent=dev-team, owner_client_session=$SESSION). That claim SUCCEEDED (claimed:true) even though the task's own developer agent is independently confirmed still alive by the harness's own background-task tracker -- meaning BOUNDED-1's own claim/dispatch step (main.md 'Idle-capacity backlog pickup' section) does not itself take (or already releases) the task:<id> sprint-task lock that S2 relies on to detect 'already resumed, do not re-spawn'. Had this router not had independent out-of-band confirmation the agent was alive, following the literal spec here (S2: claimed=true -> spawn head.next_agent) would have spawned a SECOND developer instance onto the same live task -- a genuine duplicate-spawn, the exact failure class flagged in memory feedback_pipeline_resume_stale_placeholder_duplicate_spawn_risk, now confirmed for the BOUNDED-1-originated case specifically (as opposed to the S2-originated resume case the lock design assumes).
compounding_factor: head.next_agent was left as the literal string 'dev-team' (BOUNDED-1's own bookkeeping placeholder meaning 'router resolves the specialist via zone-detect', per head.next_action text) -- NOT a real spawnable agent type. 'dev-team' has no agent type (CLAUDE.md: 'There is no dev-team agent type'). A literal Agent(head.next_agent=...) call on this head shape would fail outright on an invalid agent type, separate from and in addition to the duplicate-spawn risk above.
manual_mitigation_applied_this_tick: Router released the just-acquired task:<id> lock immediately without spawning, left .head untouched (still correctly in_progress -- BOUNDED-1/SLS/RLC/DRS correctly stay dormant this tick since head is genuinely busy), fell through to Step 1 PO Triage.
recommended_fix: Either (a) BOUNDED-1's own dispatch step should also take the task:<id> sprint-task lock (mirroring S2's dispatcher-wrap exactly) so a later tick's pipeline-resume correctly sees it held and SKIPs, or (b) Step 0b's WF-1/WF-1b/WF-1c chain should add a BOUNDED-1-origin check (e.g. head.updated_by starts with 'dev-team (bounded-1' / 'dev-team (SLS' / 'dev-team (RLC' etc.) as an additional short-circuit -- treat exactly like WF-2's supervised-hold (leave head unchanged, fall through to Step 1, do NOT attempt S2 claim/spawn at all) since these lanes' own dispatch-time claim/spawn already happened and head being in_progress IS the live-work signal, with no resume ever needed for them specifically (only genuine crash-recovery resume needs S2, and that path is for a head that was live in a PRIOR router session, not this same one).
